terms.meaning: The right to collect land revenue.
One of the Sikh groups of the late 18th century.
Wellesley's plan: a ruler kept a British army in his state and paid for it, or gave up land.
Dalhousie's rule: a king with no natural heir lost his kingdom, since adopted sons couldn't inherit.

items.name: Clive and the misrule
items.formula: Robert Clive was the first Governor of Bengal (1758); Company servants then looted openly.
items.example: The British replaced Mir Jafar with his son-in-law Mir Qasim.

items.name: Battle of Buxar (1764)
items.formula: Mir Qasim, removed for ending the dastak misuse, allied with the Nawab of Oudh and the Mughal king.
items.example: The British beat all three and grew stronger.

items.name: Grant of Diwani (1765)
items.formula: Clive's treaty with Shah Alam II: Diwani of Bengal, Bihar and Odisha for 26 lakh rupees a year.
items.example: Bengal was then heavily exploited; in the famine a third of its people died.

items.name: Regulating Act (1773)
items.formula: British Parliament's control over the Company; Warren Hastings became the first Governor General.
items.example: Pitt's India Act (1784) fixed its defects.

items.name: Anglo-Mysore wars (1767-1799)
items.formula: Four wars against Hyder Ali and Tippu Sultan.
items.example: Tippu's kingdom was split four ways: British, Nizam, Marathas and the Wodeyars.

items.name: Anglo-Maratha wars (1775-1818)
items.formula: Three wars; the Peshwa surrendered and the British abolished the post.

items.name: Ranjit Singh and the Sikh wars
items.formula: Ranjit Singh became king of Lahore at 18 and united the Sikhs; the Afghan king gave him the Kohinoor.
items.example: After his death (1839), the British won four wars and took Punjab in 1849.

items.name: Effects of the Subsidiary Alliance
items.formula: Army costs ruined the states, they lost land and sovereignty.

items.name: Effects of the Doctrine of Lapse
items.formula: Oudh, Satara, Nagpur, Jhansi and others were annexed.
items.example: By 1856, two thirds of the subcontinent was British.

mistakes.text: Subsidiary Alliance was Wellesley's; the Doctrine of Lapse was Dalhousie's.
Clive was the first Governor of Bengal; Warren Hastings was the first Governor General.
Buxar was in 1764; the Diwani was granted a year later, in 1765.
